newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore financial sector prospects bright - MAS.
newsitem.headline: Singapore financial sector prospects bright - MAS.

text.p: The prospects for Singapore's financial services industry are bright despite some problems with the region's economic growth, Lee Ek Tieng, Managing Director of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said on Tuesday.
"While there may be some problems to the region's economic growth in the near-term, economic fundamentals remain strong," Lee told bankers of the Association of Banks in Singapore.
He said East Asian economies, excluding Japan, are projected to grow at a rate of seven percent over the next two years.
Savings rates in the region remain high, supported by prudent fiscal policies, he added.
"The financial sector in Singapore will continue to expand on the back of continued economic growth in East Asia," he said.
Lee said the region continued to attract substantial foreign direct investment, resulting in abundant business opportunities for financial institutions.
"On the whole, financial institutions in Singapore were more profitable in 1996 compared with 1995," Lee said.
He said aggregate after-tax profits of the financial sector increased by 31.2 percent to Singapore $5.9 billion in 1996.
Net profit of the local banks rose 13.5 percent to S$2 billion, while foreign banks' earnings jumped by 56 percent to S$2.7 billion.
Lee said fund managers achieved the highest growth in profits of 105 percent, largely due to the rapid expansion of fund management activity from a relatively low base.
